title: How to frame cross-stitch for display
subtitle: Lacing, mounting on card, and choosing a frame
excerpt: Cross-stitch is typically framed by stretching the washed, pressed piece over acid-free card and lacing the edges on the back, then placing it into a frame. The lacing method keeps the fabric taut without glue and can be undone if the piece ever needs re-mounting.
sourceNotes: Lacing and mounting methods for embroidery framing documented in Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), Project Gutenberg #20776, finishing chapter. Standard practice unchanged since Victorian era.

glossaryTerms.definition: A framing technique in which the edges of the fabric are folded over a stiff card mount and laced together on the back with strong thread, like tightening a corset. The lacing holds the fabric taut without adhesive and can be undone if the mount needs to be changed.

content.text: Cross-stitch is framed by stretching the washed piece over a stiff mount card and securing it on the back with the
lacing method
. Lacing pulls the fabric evenly taut from all sides and is reversible. Glue and tape are faster but tend to buckle the fabric over time and are impossible to undo.
What you need
Acid-free mount card.
Cut to the aperture size of the frame, or buy ready-cut mount boards from a framers. Acid-free card prevents yellowing over decades.
Strong thread.
Linen thread, carpet thread, or a doubled length of standard sewing thread. It needs to hold tension without snapping.
A large-eyed needle and long ruler.
The needle works on the back of the mount; the ruler helps align the design squarely.
Mounting the piece
Centre the design on the mount card.
Lay the pressed piece face-down on the table. Place the card over it and align the design centrally. Use the Aida grid to check that the design is straight, not just centred by eye.
Fold the top and bottom edges over the card.

Fold the excess fabric over the top and bottom edges of the card. Thread the needle with lacing thread and work a zigzag stitch between the top and bottom margins, pulling taut as you go. This pulls the fabric tight over the card in the vertical direction.
Fold and lace the side edges.
Fold the left and right edges over the card. Lace horizontally between the side margins, adjusting tension to keep the fabric square.
Mite the corners and secure.
Fold the fabric at each corner neatly, like wrapping a parcel. Secure the corner folds with a few stitches so they do not spring open.
Fit into the frame.
Place the mounted piece into the frame. Standard box frames with a deep rebate work well for cross-stitch; the stitches sit slightly raised and do not touch the glass.
